original_card.question: What exact content and credit of a small named PR set has already been retained?
methods: Compare exact heads and retained artifacts to write a source-bound disposition receipt.
Audit an existing receipt for missing content or predecessor attribution.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Separate complete integration, partial retention and changed heads; make no autonomous closures.

first_step.inspect: Read one small PR set in the ledger and identify exact reviewed heads and unresolved content.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Compare that set to retained artifacts; produce a complete or explicitly partial disposition receipt.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Reliable overlap evidence preserves credit and prevents repeated review of already-retained material.
allowed_variations: One small related PR family or one existing integration receipt.
scope_change_triggers: Treating matching titles or one shared blob as proof of full incorporation.

actual_scope: Source-bound post-merge content-and-credit receipt for the nine PRs integrated at merge commit 51122344de9382e784c7f89953456d8cd55513ef (#1805, #1806, #1808, #1810, #1811, #1812, #1814, #1815, #1827): whether each reviewed head's own changed paths are retained byte-identically in the merged tree, whether any head changed since review, and whether author credit is recorded.
scope_change_reason: The card names no family; this refines it to one existing integration receipt (the maintainer merge of the research/community-efficient800-audit batch), the newest small named set whose post-merge retention had no receipt. Its scoped review predates the merge and records every PR as github_state OPEN, so content retention in the merged tree was an open question at selection time. Distinct from mathematical audits of individual members (for example the independent PR1805 audit and the PR1805/PR1062 composition claim of 2026-10-14), which concern mechanisms rather than merge retention.
bottleneck_link: Reliable overlap evidence preserves credit and prevents repeated review of already-retained material: this receipt certifies the nine efficient800 packages are on main byte-identically under their reviewed heads, so reviewers need not re-scan their content, and it records (without changing) the still-partial ledger dispositions. Side result: no kappa, supplier or frontier effect.
stop_rule: Stop after the nine heads' complete changed-path sets are compared against the merge tree, with rejection controls and source pins; no mathematical re-review of package contents, no ledger edits, no closures, no package replays beyond this receipt's verifier.
evidence: RECEIPT.json: 77/77 changed paths across the nine PRs retained byte-identically in the merge tree (0 modified, 0 missing), 0 changed heads versus research/community-efficient800-audit/DISPOSITIONS.json reviewed_head fields, merge parents exactly base d33f15be plus the nine reviewed heads, and all nine authors present in CONTRIBUTORS.md. research/merge5112-retention-receipt/verify.py prints PASS_MERGE5112_RETENTION_RECEIPT with source pins ok and 7/7 rejection controls.
author: Aaron Wang
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance from opencode (agent session); no independent human review claimed.

open_questions.question: Should the nine docs/research/pr-ledger.md rows move from 'partially reviewed' to 'incorporated' now that merge 51122344 retains their exact reviewed heads?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The ledger is the central review entry point; rows that understate retention make reviewers re-scan already-retained work.
open_questions.first_step: A maintainer updates the nine rows citing this receipt and research/community-efficient800-audit/DISPOSITIONS.json, keeping the scoped-review limitations on record.
open_questions.blocked_by: Disposition and closure changes are maintainer actions; this package deliberately makes none.

open_questions.question: Do the nine contributed packages' own checkers still pass on the merged tree?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Blob identity establishes content retention but not that each contributed verifier runs green in the merged repository state.
open_questions.first_step: Run each package's registered replay or verify.py under Python 3.12 from a merge-5112 checkout and record a per-package result table.
open_questions.blocked_by: Session time; several packages declare long or dependency-bearing replays that need their own bounded runs.
